title: Define marketplace refresh scope, success metrics, and acceptance criteria (AWS + GCP listings)
creator: Nikhil Sharma
project: AWS + GCP Cloud Marketplace Listing Refresh
description:
## Goal
Define the *scope*, *success metrics*, and *acceptance criteria* for the AWS + GCP marketplace refresh so teams can implement onboarding + listing updates and partner submissions without churn.

This ticket is the “north star” for what we will ship for marketplace refresh v2 and how we will measure it.

## Background / context
We are refreshing our AWS Marketplace and Google Cloud Marketplace listings to better support enterprise procurement (committed spend, PO/invoicing) while preserving a developer-first onboarding experience.

Key elements in play:
- New SKU taxonomy (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private + add-ons)
- Updated security attachments + consistent claims
- Purchase → entitlement → org linking reliability + better customer instructions
- Launch readiness: internal enablement + monitoring/support playbooks

## In scope (for this refresh)
1) Marketplace listing content refresh (AWS + GCP)
- Updated headline/long description/value props
- Updated SKU/pricing tables and consistent naming
- Updated categories/keywords and required listing fields
- Updated screenshots/diagrams (redaction as needed)
- Marketplace listing attachments/links updated (security + onboarding docs)

2) Security packet refresh and internal sign-off workflow
- Marketplace security FAQ + security packet evidence index
- Accuracy review with SecEng/GRC; avoid over-promising

3) Onboarding/provisioning improvements required for marketplace purchases
- Entitlement ingestion + mapping (AWS/GCP SKU IDs → Redwood entitlements)
- Webhook validation + audit logging for provisioning events
- Console UX for org linking + entitlement status
- Docs updates for AWS + GCP onboarding + FAQ

4) Launch readiness
- Submission/review readiness checklist, QA checklist, monitoring/alerts
- Sales/SE/CS enablement: FAQ, talk tracks, troubleshooting guide

## Out of scope
- Major runtime/inference features unrelated to marketplace onboarding
- Full billing re-platform; only minimal changes to support new SKUs and invoice descriptions

## Target buyers / personas
- Procurement-driven enterprise buyer: needs clear SKUs, compliant language, predictable invoicing via marketplace
- Technical evaluator / platform team: wants fast activation and clarity on deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Security reviewer: needs accurate claims + evidence handling process

## Success metrics (measured within 30/60/90 days post launch)
### Marketplace funnel + activation
- Marketplace-sourced opportunities created (AWS + GCP): +25% vs previous 60-day baseline
- Purchase → first successful request (activation) median time:
  - Hosted: p50 < 30 minutes, p90 < 4 hours
  - Dedicated/Private: p50 < 1 business day to “entitlement confirmed + handoff created”, p90 < 3 business days
- Entitlement activation lag (purchase event → entitlement available in Redwood):
  - p95 < 15 minutes (hosted-style flows)

### Reliability + support load
- Provisioning pipeline success rate: ≥ 99.5% (excluding customer input errors like wrong org selection)
- Webhook ingestion error rate: < 0.5% daily, with automated retries + alerting
- Support tickets attributed to “marketplace onboarding/provisioning”:
  - < 10% of total onboarding tickets post-launch
  - Top 3 categories have documented macros + runbooks

### Content + review readiness
- AWS + GCP listing review passes without “major” resubmission (i.e., no full restart due to missing required fields/attachments)
- Security packet language passes SecEng/GRC review and is consistent across: listing copy, security FAQ, docs site

### Attribution + reporting
- Marketplace lead attribution is captured end-to-end (UTM/source + marketplace identifier where available) into CRM lifecycle stages.

## Acceptance criteria
### A) AWS Marketplace listing (content + attachments)
1) Listing fields complete and internally approved
- Headline + short description + long description use approved messaging framework
- Supported deployment modes clearly described (Hosted API / Dedicated / Private) with no ambiguity
- SKU names match the SKU catalog + internal billing plan codes naming conventions
- Keywords/categories updated per AWS guidelines

2) Attachments and links
- Links to onboarding docs page (AWS-specific) and customer FAQ are correct and non-404
- Security packet attachment present (or linked per AWS requirement) with correct disclaimers
- Support contact + escalation instructions included (customer-facing)

3) Claims governance
- No unapproved security/compliance claims (e.g., “HIPAA compliant”) without explicit sign-off
- “Shared responsibility” statement included in FAQ/attachment or listing where appropriate

4) Screenshots/diagrams
- Screenshots reflect current Console UI and include marketplace org linking + entitlement status
- Any redaction required is applied and approved

### B) GCP Marketplace listing (content + deployment steps)
1) Listing copy matches GCP formatting and requirements
- Solution description uses approved messaging blocks
- Deployment/provisioning steps are accurate for GCP flow (including validation specifics)
- SKU taxonomy is consistent with AWS + Redwood Console naming (allowing for GCP formatting differences)

2) Policies + required links
- Required GCP policy links included (privacy, support, terms where applicable)
- Security FAQ link present and accurate

3) Validation + provisioning
- The “how to get started” flow accounts for region constraints and calls out known limitations
- Clear guidance for org linking and what identifiers customers need to provide

### C) Cross-cloud consistency requirements
- SKU naming consistency across: AWS listing, GCP listing, Redwood Console, internal billing
- Support docs include “AWS vs GCP differences” section (at minimum: purchase steps, entitlement timing expectations, region constraints)
- A single internal review checklist exists and is used for final sign-off

## Definition of Done
- Success metrics and baselines recorded and shared with stakeholders (PMM, Partnerships, Eng, Support)
- Acceptance criteria reviewed in working session with: Partnerships (marketplace owner), PMM, Eng lead, SecEng/GRC, Support
- Criteria embedded into the launch readiness checklist and used as gate for submission

- Onboarding flow spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/marketplace-purchase-to-provisioning-onboarding-flow.json

## Open questions (resolved in comments)
- What is the minimum acceptable entitlement activation SLA for launch?
- How do we define “activation” for Dedicated/Private (handoff vs first request)?
- Which security evidence can be attached vs shared under NDA only?
comments: 2025-01-16 — Soojin Lee: Confirmed we should use one cross-cloud messaging spine, but allow formatting differences. Requested explicit “what you get” bullets per SKU family plus a short procurement-oriented section (committed spend, invoicing).

2025-01-17 — Dr. Aisha Rahman: Flagged we must avoid any hard compliance claims in listing copy. Recommended consistent language: “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA” and “encryption in transit/at rest” with KMS integration described as “supported” where applicable.

2025-01-20 — Rafael Mendes: Proposed reliability metrics to include p95 entitlement lag and webhook error rate with alerts. Asked that this ticket define thresholds that map to SRE dashboards so we don’t debate at launch.

2025-01-21 — Ben Carter: Confirmed attribution plan: UTMs + marketplace source tagging into HubSpot lifecycle stages. Requested metric definition: ‘marketplace-sourced pipeline’ includes opportunities created where primary source = AWS Marketplace / GCP Marketplace within 14 days of first marketplace touch.

2025-01-23 — Lauren Bishop: Dedicated/Private activation definition: ‘activation’ for those SKUs should be “entitlement confirmed + provisioning request created + owner assigned” (since first inference may happen later). Agree to measure time-to-handoff separately from time-to-first-token.

2025-01-24 — Marcus Lin: Acceptance criteria update: include explicit requirement for audit logging wording to match current capabilities (provisioning events + console admin actions logged; customer app-level logs depend on integration). Approved proposed claim governance section.

2025-01-28 — Nikhil Sharma: Consolidated scope + metrics + acceptance criteria; reviewed with Partnerships + PMM + Sec + SRE in working session. Marking Done; criteria will be referenced as gate in PM-875 launch checklist.
